findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate the audit-log datetime field
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to the ordering value. The audit-log endpoint selects this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, so once results are fetched, `value` is a `datetime` and cursor construction raises `TypeError`. Any administrator using `optimized_pagination=true` on this endpoint will receive a 500 response. This paginator needs datetime key conversion equivalent to `DateTimePaginator`, or the endpoint must use a paginator compatible with datetime ordering.

findings.title: Changing existing span buffer keys from sets to sorted sets has no rollout compatibility
findings.body: This now writes `ZADD` to the existing `span-buf:s:*` keys, while buffers created by the currently deployed version are Redis Sets. Redis will return WRONGTYPE for `ZADD` (and the new Lua script's `ZCARD`) until every old key expires, causing `process_spans` batches for affected traces to fail and preventing those spans from being buffered. A production rollout needs a key-version/migration strategy or compatibility handling for old Set keys during the Redis TTL window.

findings.title: Configured max_segment_spans is ignored and replaced by a hard-coded eviction limit
findings.body: `SpansBuffer` still exposes and stores `max_segment_spans`, but the Lua script always retains 1000 members and receives no configured limit argument. Deployments which set a different `max_segment_spans` value will silently have their configuration ignored; unlike the prior behavior, excess data is also silently evicted rather than detected and skipped by `_load_segment_data`. Pass the configured limit to the script (and define the intended overflow behavior) or remove the unsupported configuration contract.
